item: D5 Selection of the reported result
support_quote: comprises three subscales: individual reasons, environmental reasons, and amotivation
reasoning: Decided by the user on 2026-11-28 (gate 3, Q1, sentence (a); protocol amendment A10): reporting only the total or composite score of an instrument whose subscales the Methods name is rated Some concerns under D5, unless a registration or protocol named the subscales as outcomes; how the total was formed is rated under D4. The rating is the user's ruling, not the adjudicator's. The adjudicator had escalated this item, and its reasoning was: Both judges read the paper correctly. The Methods describe the MSPPA's three subscales and its total ('scored from 16 to 80'), and the Results give only the total. Judge 1's second ground, selection among analyses, does not meet any High clause as written: those clauses name outcome, time point and subscales. The absolute, change-score and ANCOVA results are all reported, and only the Abstract's emphasis differs. So the rating turns only on whether a total reported in place of the subscales is 'only some of the subscales', which is the same question escalated for pm-40567995. The registration predates recruitment, but its content is not in the saved text, so Low is not shown either way. The user's question is the same: does a total or composite reported in place of every subscale the Methods describe meet D5 High?

support_quote: The MSPPA is a validated 16-item, 5-point Likert-type scale scored from 16 to 80 that measures motivation to participate in physical activity and comprises three subscales: individual reasons, environmental reasons, and amotivation [ 14 ].
reasoning: Ratified by the user on 2026-11-28 (ruling given after the audit) under amendment A11 as written: the paper gives the score's range but does not say whether the amotivation items are reverse-scored, so the code is other. The pipeline had sent this value back to the judges and adjudicator without an instruction from the user; the user ratified the adjudicator's decision, which is now the user's ruling. The adjudicator's reasoning was: Every between-group test is on the MSPPA total. The 16-to-80 range implies the items are summed, but the paper never says whether the amotivation items are reverse-scored, and unlike the WRVAS it never says which direction of the total is higher, so its valence does not follow from the stated formation. Under amendment A11(a) the code is other, not favours exergame. The authors' reading ('smaller decline in motivation') is a conclusion, and section 7 codes from the test.
